Return only JSON choices with short editorial purpose text, no traveler answer prose or copied source facts. Use each source role exactly. The choices array has a strict maximum of four references TOTAL, including any cash benchmark; that is a ceiling, not a target to fill. Use no duplicate references and at most one b. Choose a small useful comparison pool and a direct cash benchmark when available. When complete journeys exist, include a partial lead only if it adds distinct decision value; usually none is needed. With no complete journey, choose 2–3 relevant leads plus cash context when available. Select defensibly from route, timing, reported cabin scope, traveler and seat evidence, fare scope, costs and caveats. Points across programs are not comparable economic costs. The selected choices will receive exact source facts before writing. No complete eligible journey exists; choose a relevant l when leads exist. Do not treat a date-only lead as a timed itinerary. The selected set is evidence for the final writer, not the final list of recommendations. It may contain a comparator that the writer discusses as an alternative. Ranking highlight/index arrays indicate membership, not an order of preference; compare their facts rather than assuming the first listed is best. Begin with Ranking highlights, then examine the full eligible inventory for material same-program timing, fee and connection-buffer alternatives, plus different cabin, route or separate-ticket risk. A later arrival with the same program, cabin and observed amount needs a concrete traveler benefit before it becomes the lead. Include an earlier-arriving same-program journey when its schedule is a meaningful comparison, even if another variant departs at a different time. Do not fill a count or cabin quota, and avoid near-identical siblings that teach no new tradeoff. One complete journey can suffice only when no other eligible choice supplies a useful comparator. For an incomplete-only answer, choose leads whose reported date, seats, fees or program show a useful next-check contrast; these remain leads, never complete itineraries. Preserve unknown price scope, traveler support and separate-ticket protection. The writer sees only the selected source facts, so retain material comparison evidence. The exact_details index supplies source-bound journey_components, per-journey separate-booking waits, factored award-itinerary connections, and nonlead component original-currency quotes in major units. Lead original-currency quotes are in each lead_records entry's original_quote object. Use these exact references to distinguish within-award layovers from separate-ticket connection waits; they have different risk meanings. Compare reported fee and cash amounts using the display value and currency, never mental division of raw minor units. A quote with unknown price_scope is neither per traveler nor a party total, even if returned traveler evidence is known. Unknown wait_minutes is not zero. Keep a comparator when its exact buffer, schedule, cabin or quote changes the decision; no fixed count applies. For each selected choice, also return purpose: one short editorial hypothesis about why this exact choice helps the traveler decide, and compare_to: another selected exact alias or null. The output choice is {k:'j'|'b'|'l',r:exact alias,purpose:short text,compare_to:exact selected other alias or null}. Choose a comparison target when it helps reveal a concrete supported gain and real loss; otherwise null. Describe an intended traveler decision in purpose, not a new source value, repeated number or invented traveler preference. Do not choose near-identical siblings merely to fill the pool. If a same-program, same-cabin cousin looks worse on schedule and price, select it only for a source-supported offsetting traveler benefit. These purposes are unverified writing suggestions, not source facts or final recommendations. The composer must recheck every claim against each selected record and may reject a suggested purpose. With no complete journey, look for a supported lead-to-lead difference that changes the next check: reported program, date, seat evidence or same-program quote with comparable currency and scope. In each useful purpose, name the lead's potential upside and its real tradeoff against another selected lead. A shared missing schedule is not a benefit. Keep direct cash as a separate baseline, not a substitute for a useful lead comparison. There is no lead count or cabin quota; one lead is enough when no other source-supported contrast helps the traveler. These purposes remain unverified hypotheses for the composer to check. In this selector packet, journey_records are keyed by exact J alias. Each record names its JP profile, exact award/cash component refs, and repeats that journey's reported award cabin, program and points. Component_records use exact A/C aliases and CP profiles. Read a record's named profile for its other facts. JP and CP are data profiles, never selectable source aliases. The inline fields retain their source scope and do not establish leg cabins or total cost. For incomplete leads, favor differences that could change which lead the traveler checks first, such as a reported date, program, or truly comparable original quote. There is no program, date, or count quota. A surplus reported seat count above the requested party is not by itself a traveler benefit. Do not compare points across programs as economic value, or prices across currencies or unknown scopes as total savings. Keep purpose text an unverified selector hypothesis. In this incomplete-only selector view, lead_records replaces lead_rows. Each ordered lead record names the former lead_row fields. Other component quotes remain in exact_details.component_quotes.
Write for the traveler. Call the supplied material search results, not a packet or an internal validation workflow. Report amounts as source quotes and preserve unknown scope. Use same or equal only when the source values are exactly equal; when rounding small differences, say approximately or nearly rather than implying exact equality.

For example, if a shown reference starts J14@, put the standalone token J14 in visible narrative prose. Keep the typed reference blocks and source facts correct. In the correction task, identified by an input JSON previous_wire key, remove that internal short identifier from all traveler-visible prose and labels, apply the supplied checker feedback, and preserve the useful answer. Do not add a new identifier on correction.
